brief.name: Dext
brief.summary: Dext is a Visual Studio Code extension for AI conversations and typed workflows. It activates on startup and composes a host extension around a sidebar chat plus editor-tab webviews. Users choose Ask, Agent, Plan, or Code: Ask explores code without edits, Agent delegates implementation, Plan creates and revises a plan then continues it with Build, and Code writes TypeScript workflows with typed API completion and diagnostics. Dext manages conversation tabs, workspace references and attachments, streaming transcripts with agent traces and todo progress, input questions, patch review, and conversation history. AI turns are routed to separately installed and authenticated Codex CLI, Claude CLI, or DeepSeek Harness backends using the selected CLI's credentials. Workflow callables are cataloged as generated Dext APIs and can run in a long-lived Node child process. MCP tools are called over stdio JSON-RPC, HTTP, or REST. A project knowledge workspace collects bounded evidence, indexes structure, generates intent and C4/diagram views, and serves them in a reader; a packaged Archify runtime is launched as a Node subprocess for diagram validation and rendering.

capabilities.description: VS Code activation and host composition, plus the sidebar and editor-tab shell that carries Dext's UI. It constructs the application and project services, registers commands and providers, manages panel creation, reuse, restoration and CSP-governed HTML, routes validated webview messages, and holds responses until the sidebar view is ready.

Host and browser conversation state for open tabs, saved history and preferences, with turn execution, cancellation and plan continuation. It brokers agent questions, elicitation forms and UI interactions, tracks per-turn patches for review and application, and coordinates one active run per conversation while routing events, answers, patch results and plan rounds.

Routes AI requests to Codex, Claude or DeepSeek Harness profiles and discovers their models and defaults. It manages DeepSeek Harness launch, session, permission and sandbox policy, applies shared agent permissions through a bounded workspace terminal handler, and compiles callable contracts into structured generations with result recovery, repair and assertion checks.

Built-in and project callable catalog, generated Dext declarations, static API reference extraction, workflow templates, and conversation recording. Shared execution contracts and the host/Node kernel execute Code-mode TypeScript, validate and dispatch typed API calls, serialize results across boundaries, and replay recorded calls.

Conversation composer and its workspace context surface. It keeps per-conversation drafts and attachment chips, edits references in Monaco with TypeScript completion and theme support, searches workspace files and project objects, stages copied selections and files, builds content-hashed code references, and applies ignore and attachment-size rules.

Browser-side turn and output rendering. It builds turn disclosures, headers, process and output sections and actions, renders messages, reasoning traces, grouped tool activity and todo progress, classifies links, maintains follow-at-end scrolling, and formats Markdown, Mermaid, JSON, code and durations.

Project knowledge lifecycle from bounded evidence collection and structure indexing through AI-generated intent, knowledge and diagrams, persisted project documents, architecture rules and the Overview, Knowledge and Diagrams reader. It derives C4, structure and class views, serves graph queries, validates diagram output, tracks model continuity and stores diagram snapshots.

Authoring and browsing for Dext resources and tool integrations. It models API, MCP, rule, skill and template resources, discovers SKILL.md packages, renders resource catalogs and documents, and parses MCP manifests to invoke tools over stdio, HTTP or REST while storing scoped access tokens in host secret storage.

contexts.purpose: VS Code activation and host composition root. The packaged main (dist/extension.js, onStartupFinished) enters extension.ts, which constructs DextApplication, loads declarations and project settings, and wires history, sidebar, project/resource tabs, commands, watchers and trust/config reloads. projectSetup registers Project pages, the AI provider, diagram registry, evidence readers and tab restoration; application assembles runtime, kernel, MCP, skills and agent services.

Host and browser conversation state. conversationSetup assembles the controller, turn coordinator, event stream and interaction, plan and patch services; the host controller owns open and active tabs, hydration, layout persistence and per-tab selection; preferences persist pins, favorites, titles, sort and filter settings and selections; domain rules order sessions and normalize layouts; browser modules keep render identity, view caches and the draggable tab strip.

contexts.canonicalName: Agent Execution Routing and CLI Backends
contexts.purpose: Agent execution routing and CLI backends. DefaultAgentRunner dispatches Codex, Claude or DeepSeek Harness requests by profile; the CLI runner builds provider arguments, streams output, parses structured and conversational results, tracks todos and tool activity and enforces total and idle timeouts. The Codex conversation path adds app-server JSON-RPC, event translation and error mapping.

contexts.canonicalName: DeepSeek Harness Runtime and ACP Transport
contexts.purpose: DeepSeek Harness lifecycle and ACP boundary. Resolves CLI or desktop launch assets, installation presets and model/default policy; applies permission and sandbox rules; binds and resumes ACP sessions and turns; serves an authenticated loopback bridge for questions and result-tool registration; supplies the default preset and structured-result fallback envelope.

Agent input requests. Converts elicitation JSON schemas into typed form fields and Harness question frames into Dext question and answer cards, rejecting unsafe or unrepresentable schemas; the browser view preserves drafts, renders pending question cards and interaction forms, and dispatches answers.

contexts.canonicalName: Agent Message, Trace and Todo Rendering
contexts.purpose: Presentation of agent turn output. Builds message sections, changes and references, prepares history traces, renders live execution traces with reasoning and grouped tool activity, and derives todo progress labels, rows and browser todo views.

contexts.canonicalName: Structured Generation, Result Boundaries and Repair
contexts.purpose: Structured generation and result handling. Compiles callable contracts into Ax signatures with Zod and JSON Schema, exposes CLI agents through AxAIService, recovers candidate JSON from raw text, serializes results across agent and kernel boundaries, evaluates assertion snapshots and patch expectations, and runs bounded AI-assisted repair.

contexts.canonicalName: Workflow Callable Catalog, Typings and Runtime
contexts.purpose: Built-in Dext workflow catalog and executor. Defines callable metadata and provider-specific CLI fields, renders generated dext declarations, typings and workspace files, reports missing declarations, validates and dispatches Dext API calls to deterministic handlers or agent CLIs, normalizes and repairs results, and serves Ask, Agent, Plan and structured-JSON turns.

Workspace context and attachments. Defines text snapshots and the ContextHost port; resolves file, symbol and directory references; captures and validates editor selections, workspace or external files and clipboard paths; opens documents and links; and applies Dext attachment and plan storage policy with size limits.

Code execution across the extension host and Node kernel. Spawns and handshakes with a long-lived kernel, defines parent and kernel wire messages, dispatches API calls with bounded concurrency and cancellation, runs the user module and captures output, records calls for resume replay, and silences TypeScript-stripping warnings.

Canonical cross-feature execution contract surface. Declares invocation, callable, UI, MCP, terminal, patch, agent-input, stream and runtime shapes, and provides Zod result and wire-step schemas used at kernel and agent boundaries.

contexts.canonicalName: Project Knowledge Model and AI Generation
contexts.purpose: Versioned project knowledge model and its AI generation pipeline. Defines workspace paths, tool and evidence settings and intent, knowledge, provenance and ownership schemas; packages bounded repository evidence, bridges the selected agent runtime, validates generated intent and diagrams, checkpoints resumable initialization, and reports model-quality concerns.

contexts.canonicalName: Project Structure Indexing and Graph Analysis
contexts.purpose: Host-side project structure index. Parses workspace source and configuration into a versioned, cache-aware set of symbols, imports and resolved dependencies, then derives file consumers, dependency edges, ranks, communities, cycles, hubs and bounded structural facts.

Project diagram model and rendering runtime. Defines diagram and architecture-view shapes with structural validation, derives bounded structure and type maps from indexed facts, and provides adapter registration, rendering, cancellation, validation receipts, last-good snapshots, history and viewer export safeguards.

Composer input and attachment editing for conversations. Stores per-conversation drafts with attachment chips, observes the compact composer action row for overflow, and computes source-preserving text and cursor edits for reference insertion, pasted content, drag-and-drop paths, and reference removal.

Shared workspace and project reference capability. Parses @file, range, and project-object tokens; validates and formats reference paths and chip descriptors; searches accepted project objects and intent entries; and provides host-side ranking plus a latest-query browser client for workspace file lookup.

Interactive agent-input lifecycle. Validates shared UI-form schemas, brokers pending questions and UI interactions on the host, routes notifications and focus, and renders modal browser forms with Markdown, selects, grouped choices, and secret-safe controls.

Patch proposal lifecycle spanning browser review, conversation host, and VS Code application. Tracks per-turn unapplied patches, renders accept and reject controls and diff rows, validates changed ranges against document hashes, applies edits, and shares patch-result parsing.

Running-turn execution boundary for conversations. Defines execution snapshots and host ports, enforces one active run per conversation, owns abort and plan continuation, routes agent events and plan rounds, persists provider sessions, and exposes the shared cancellation error.

Live conversation reading surface. Builds turn disclosures, headers, process and output sections, per-turn actions, and editable titles with plan hydration; provides HTML and DOM turn rendering plus external and workspace link classification; and maintains follow-at-end scrolling, jump controls, viewport corrections, and scroll diagnostics.

Plan-mode lifecycle. Separates plan documents from streamed response text, derives plan names and paths, tracks execution rounds and todo progress, orchestrates host plan sessions and continuation, and renders the Plan toolbar's target, status, and build controls.

Persisted conversation state and History reader. Defines session and turn records with bounded retention, normalizes saved responses, specifies per-conversation preferences, hosts the History editor, and renders saved turns as HTML or Markdown with actions, plans, diffs, and terminal output.

Resource authoring model. Defines resource kinds and scopes, labels and directories, filenames and safe path segments, editable target/draft/session state, generation prompts, bounded supporting-file validation, and merge rules for APIs, MCP manifests, rules, skills, templates, and ordinary files before writes reach the workspace.

MCP server integration. Defines server, tool, transport, and credential contracts; parses committed JSONC manifests into tools, methods, and diagnostics; applies HTTP and loopback URL rules; registers and executes stdio, streamable HTTP, and REST calls; and stores scoped access tokens in host secret storage.

Project evidence and initialization lifecycle. Defines normalized evidence, inventory, limits, progress, and resumable checkpoint contracts; collects bounded workspace documentation, manifests, source excerpts, structure indexes, and Archify metadata; and runs initialization from preparation through generation and save with cancellation, retry, output tailing, and stale-run protection.

Project structure intelligence. Reads cached structure summaries and dependency graphs, indexes workspace inputs into bounded source evidence, checks browser build entries and runtime-boundary windows, reports startup gaps, derives responsibility and knowledge candidates, writes the structure cache, and serves graph queries through a read-only stdio MCP server.

Versioned project document persistence. Defines Zod schemas and canonical paths for project definitions, intent, evidence, diagrams, objects, architecture, and history; enforces expected-version checks on saves; and adapts the VS Code workspace filesystem for reads, writes, and directory listing.

contexts.canonicalName: Project Knowledge Topics and Model Continuity
contexts.purpose: Project knowledge topics and model continuity. Builds knowledge topics from project intent, diagrams, C4 landscape and runtime-unit views, checks evidence freshness, fingerprints topics, and reconciles regenerated models with prior identities and analysis history.

contexts.canonicalName: Project Architecture Rules and Reader Notes
contexts.purpose: Architecture governance and reader notes. Evaluates declared allow, deny, and no-cycle rules against project diagrams, reports violations and evaluation notes, and renders rules, violations, and decisions as reader-facing notes.

Diagram generation and version history. Defines adapter capabilities and artifacts, runs Archify output through a host subprocess and temporary files with validation and receipts, converts architecture, structure, class, workflow, sequence, data-flow, and lifecycle models, and stores snapshots with semantic, evidence, artifact, and layout comparison across versions.

Project knowledge reader and editor. Composes settings, evidence, intent, architecture, diagrams, and initialization progress in the host data source; manages the project editor tab; and renders Overview, Knowledge, and Diagrams pages with settings, topic, gallery, architecture, and sandboxed Archify views.

contexts.canonicalName: Editor Tab Lifecycle and Document Shell
contexts.purpose: Editor-tab infrastructure and document shell for Dext panels. Defines stable tab identity, page vocabulary, titles, and validated serialized state; manages panel creation, reuse, adoption, and close; restores tabs; and renders CSP-governed HTML documents with embedded frames for sandboxed webviews.

Editor-tab browser for callable APIs and global resources. Defines resource catalog entries, list and detail data sources, panel options, and tree/search state; assembles callable, file, and Node/JavaScript reference entries; retains per-page scope, query, navigation and scroll state; renders signatures, source previews, and MCP, rule or skill documents; and routes refresh, open, copy, scope and reference commands.

contexts.canonicalName: API Reference Catalog and Static Source Analysis
contexts.purpose: Static API documentation support. Defines the Node/JavaScript reference model; validates and lazily loads the build-generated declaration catalog with version and malformed-file rejection; extracts exported TypeScript function signatures and JSDoc through Tree-sitter without executing workspace code; and provides a cached WASM grammar loader for syntax parsing.

Workflow callable catalog and signature formatting. Maintains the mutable built-in, global and project registry with source precedence, replacement rules and revision tracking, and formats field types, defaults, parameters and result types for generated declarations, runtime dispatch and API browsing, including conversation APIs whose internal fields remain caller-facing.

Typed workflow template support. YAML front matter declares the output format and string, lines or enum fields; Markdown or literal bodies render values while preserving template structure; JSON, TOML and YAML results are syntax-checked; and output schemas, presets, caller instructions and final field values are derived.

Converts recorded conversation turns into an editable TypeScript workflow skeleton. It derives an API and file name, lifts repeated prompt text into shared parameters, emits Ask, Plan and Agent steps with confirmation gates, preserves unsupported Code-mode turns as comments, and selects imports and result types.

Discovers Dext SKILL.md packages across project, configured shared and global roots, exposes precedence-aware metadata and stable descriptors, and loads instruction content with workspace-containment checks.

Monaco-based conversation composer editor: chat and code mode switching, TypeScript and plain-text models, keyboard submission, atomic projection and decoration of context references over readable source, clipboard code-reference paste conversion, file-drop insertion, diagnostics, and editor theme application.

Monaco runtime foundation for the composer: initializes workers and language contributions, routes the TypeScript worker, installs compiler defaults, injects the generated Dext declaration and workspace API modules, and derives import-aware API completion symbols from those sources.

Latest-query-wins webview transport for project-object search: posts search requests to the host, resolves superseded queries empty, correlates results by request ID, reports host errors, and clears pending work on dispose.

Cross-layer editor theming for the composer and conversation source: reads the active VS Code TextMate theme and token color customizations in the host, normalizes token styles through a shared contract, and applies them as Monaco theme rules and UI colors.

Stages copied selections and Explorer file-copy paths for later paste matching under byte limits and short expiry, and converts resolved text snapshots into content-hashed CodeRef values carrying URI, range, symbol, document version and content.

Gitignore-style workspace path filtering: parses comments, negation, directory-only patterns, anchoring, wildcards and double-star segments into ordered matchers, then applies later-rule precedence to decide whether a workspace-relative path is ignored.

Defines the shared read-only, workspace-write and full-access agent permission vocabulary, and provides the deterministic VS Code terminal handler that confines commands to a trusted local workspace with cwd containment, timeout and output bounds, validated environment overrides, and captured results.

Node-side Code-mode runtime and module loader: maps dext and dext/api imports, loads workspace TypeScript and JavaScript with a fresh per-run module graph, tracks direct workflow calls, dispatches typed API requests, enforces the cross-process JSON value rule, waits for in-flight work, and supports recorded-call replay.

Generic readiness-gated message queue: buffers messages while a consumer is marked not ready, releases the pending batch when readiness is restored, exposes readiness, and supports clearing. The sidebar host uses it to hold webview responses until the view is ready.

Host and browser boundary of the Dext sidebar. The host provider owns view lifecycle, CSP and HTML shell, validated request dispatch, conversation-service construction, composer types, resource/MCP/attachment/file-search actions and clipboard bridges; conversation state stays in the session runtime. Shared contracts define sidebar state and request/response unions; the browser shell binds DOM controls and the clipboard client correlates replies.

Agent profile and model-choice configuration. Defines profile, provider, model-option, preset and selection contracts; discovers configured Codex and Claude defaults and reads Codex model caches with resilient TOML parsing; presentation helpers choose default model, reasoning-effort and speed options for the composer.

Shared browser-side output rendering and formatting: Mermaid diagram rendering, Markdown code-block copy controls, Monaco-based conversation source colorization, JSON result formatting and compact elapsed-duration labels.

qualityIssues.message: src/features/project/host/persistence/projectInitializationCheckpointStore.ts is grouped under 'Project Evidence and Initialization', but its only non-type import consumer is src/app/projectSetup.ts in 'Extension Activation and Host Composition'. Review the responsibility boundary; imports alone do not prove ownership.

src/features/agents/presentation/agentSelectionDefaults.ts is grouped under 'Agent Profiles and Model Selection', but its only non-type import consumer is src/webview/main.ts in 'Sidebar Webview Boundary and Shell'. Review the responsibility boundary; imports alone do not prove ownership.
qualityIssues.reason: Retained. presentAgentSelection is a pure presentation function whose parameter and result types are agent-profile/model-selection vocabulary from src/features/agents/contracts/agent.ts (AgentProfile, AgentModelOption, AgentSelection); it derives the model label and default reasoning-effort and speed values. The profile store, configured Codex/Claude defaults and cache-derived model options live in src/features/agents/host/agentProfiles.ts, so the selection policy belongs to the agents feature. src/webview/main.ts is the only non-type importer and the browser composition point; a sole composing caller does not turn agent-selection policy into shell logic, and the shell's stated purpose (lifecycle, CSP, dispatch, clipboard) does not include model-selection defaulting.

qualityIssues.message: src/features/conversations/browser/composerOverflow.ts is grouped under 'Composer Editing and Attachments', but its only non-type import consumer is src/webview/main.ts in 'Sidebar Webview Boundary and Shell'. Review the responsibility boundary; imports alone do not prove ownership.

src/features/conversations/browser/conversationTabDrag.ts is grouped under 'Conversation Session, Tabs and Preferences', but its only non-type import consumer is src/webview/main.ts in 'Sidebar Webview Boundary and Shell'. Review the responsibility boundary; imports alone do not prove ownership.

src/features/workspace/browser/outputLink.ts is grouped under 'Conversation Transcript and Turn Rendering', but its only non-type import consumer is src/webview/main.ts in 'Sidebar Webview Boundary and Shell'. Review the responsibility boundary; imports alone do not prove ownership.

src/platform/browser/markdownDiagrams.ts is grouped under 'Conversation and History Output Rendering', but its only non-type import consumer is src/features/conversations/browser/interactionMarkdown.ts in 'Agent Input Interaction Lifecycle'. Review the responsibility boundary; imports alone do not prove ownership.

src/shared/lib/jsonOutput.ts is grouped under 'Conversation and History Output Rendering', but its only non-type import consumer is src/features/conversations/presentation/turnComponents.ts in 'Conversation Transcript and Turn Rendering'. Review the responsibility boundary; imports alone do not prove ownership.

src/webview/sourceHighlight.ts is grouped under 'Conversation and History Output Rendering', but its only non-type import consumer is src/webview/main.ts in 'Sidebar Webview Boundary and Shell'. Review the responsibility boundary; imports alone do not prove ownership.
qualityIssues.reason: Retained. colorizeSource is a single browser DOM colorization routine (an element plus an optional language, returning void); its work is producing highlighted source output, which matches the output-rendering responsibility, and it carries none of the sidebar boundary's view lifecycle, validated dispatch, CSP, shell state or clipboard concerns. src/webview/main.ts is its sole consumer and the composition point that renders the shell; a sole caller there is not proof of shell ownership. The boundary as supplied is coherent, so the file stays with rendering rather than being moved solely to satisfy the import heuristic.

qualityIssues.message: Files that import each other form one graph community, but they are split across 49 responsibility modules (largest: 'Agent Input Interaction Lifecycle'). Compare the module boundaries with these tightly coupled files; the graph is a navigation signal, not proof that the split is wrong.

'Workflow Kernel and Dext Runtime' spans 2 import communities, and its largest cohesive group is 2/5 files. Check whether distinct features were merged into one module; this is a review signal, not an ownership error.
